answers.brief_reasoning: Equipment: the disk on its frictionless axle, a light string wrapped around the rim, a set of known slotted masses with a hanger, a balance, and a motion detector (or a photogate on the pulley/disk, or a meterstick and stopwatch). Procedure: (1) Measure m with the balance and hang it from the string. (2) Release it from rest. (3) Record its position against time with the motion detector and take a as the slope of the velocity–time graph. If using a meterstick and stopwatch instead, time the fall through a measured height h and use a = 2h/t². (4) Change the independent variable by adding masses to the hanger, using at least 5 values of m, and repeat. To reduce uncertainty in a: do several trials for each mass and average them, or fit the slope of the v–t graph over many data points rather than using a single timing.
